source_title: Professional Call of Duty Player Arrested - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Former professional Call of Duty player Donovan "Temp" Laroda has been arrested by a Texas police department, citing reports of domestic violence as the reason for his arrest. Temp had played Call of Duty professionally for more than 10 years at the time of his arrest.
As one of the biggest shooter franchises in gaming, Call of Duty has developed a robust competitive scene across its many annual releases. The series has been at the center of some of the biggest tournaments in gaming since its inception, including iconic tournament promoters like Gfinity and Major League Gaming. Activision has also run the Call of Duty League as a professional circuit for the game since its inaugural season in 2020, featuring major esports organizations like FaZe , Cloud9, and G2 Esports. However, one former professional Call of Duty player has now found himself facing criminal charges.
The Irving Police Department reported the arrest of Donovan "Temp" Laroda in connection with an incident on October 14, 2026. The report states that police officers arrested the professional Call of Duty player in response to a possible domestic violence call, with a warrant issued for Domestic Violence Aggravated Assault, alleging the assault caused serious bodily injury to the victim. The report did not include further details about how the injury occurred, and it did not name the victim. The Irving police report does reveal that a handgun was found on the premises during the investigation, though it was not confirmed whether the firearm was connected to the incident.
Temp's charges could result in serious fines and even extended jail time if he is convicted. The charges from the Irving Police Department were labeled as a second-degree felony, which could come with anywhere from two to twenty years of prison time if he is convicted. The charges also carry a sizable fine that Temp would be required to pay out, with the former Call of Duty pro liable for as much as $10,000 in fines. Temp has not made any official public statements about the domestic violence charges following his arrest.

The charges are a major blemish on Temp's long career in the Call of Duty pro scene. Temp has competed for a variety of well-regarded esports organizations throughout his time on the professional circuit, including stints with New York Subliners, Paris Legion, and Breaking Point. Temp found significant success during his Call of Duty pro career as well, including a win as head coach of Bush Gaming at the Call of Duty Challengers Atlanta Open in May 2026. Recent years have seen Temp largely step away from an active player role, serving mainly as a coach and content creator.
The Call of Duty franchise recently welcomed the launch of its newest annual title, returning to a popular subseries. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 debuted on October 23 as the final game of the rebooted Modern Warfare series, focusing on a reignited conflict on the Korean peninsula. Modern Warfare 4 has already performed better on Steam than 2025's Black Ops 7 , though it has still failed to meet the numbers set by Black Ops 6 , which peaked at more than 300,000 players following its release in October 2024. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 will usher in the end of an era for the franchise as Activision gears up for new things on the horizon.
